nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالسَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw of oath. وَالطَّارِقِ is conjoined to it; [it is] from their saying طرق طروقا, when one comes by night.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: The exegetes hold that it [الرجع] is the rain, because it returns every year — except Ibn Zayd, who said: وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ — its sun, its moon and its stars. The plural of رجع is رجعان, heard from the Arabs, not according to analogy; if analogy were followed, one would say أرجع and رجوع.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ,] because it splits open with plants.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: [إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ is] the answer to the second oath, i.e. possessing decisiveness; and likewise وَما هُوَ بِالْهَزْلِ (14).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: That is, against the Prophet ﷺ and the believers.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [رُوَيْداً is] a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a gentle respite. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās about «رويدا»: he said: He is saying: near [in time]. Al-Ḥasan said: a little.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t:
النَّجْمُ is in the sense of "it is the piercing star". It is also possible that الثَّاقِبُ is a naʿt (adjective) of الطارق. The soundest that has been said about the meaning of الثاقب is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās about الثاقب: he said:
He is saying: the shining one. Al-Farrāʾ reported: ثقب means "it rose high", and that it is Saturn; it was called الثاقب because of its height. Someone else said: [it was so called] because of its rising from the east, as though it pierces its place.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī. Abū Jaʿfar and al-Ḥasan read إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ (4). [Translator's note: the source prints both readings as «لَمَّا»; the undoubled mīm of the first is supplied according to the explanation that follows.] Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is clear in Arabic: ما is redundant (zāʾida) and «إن» is lightened from the heavy [إنّ]; this is the school of Sībawayh, and it is the answer to the oath. In the second reading «لمّا» has the sense of "except": [no soul but has] over it [a guardian]. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh reported: أقسمت عليك لمّا فعلت, meaning "I adjure you, [do nothing] but do it". [Translator's note: the source glosses this as «ألا فعلت», apparently for «إلا فعلت».]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: [فَلْيَنْظُرِ is] from the seeing of the heart. The original is فَلِيَنظر; the kasra [of the lām] was dropped because of its heaviness, the verb is jussive by the lām of command, and the rāʾ takes a kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. مِمَّ خُلِقَ: the original is مِمّا; the alif was dropped because it is interrogative. The statement is complete [here].

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ is that the meaning of دافق is مدفوق (poured out). He [al-Farrāʾ] said: The people of the Ḥijāz are those who do this most: they bring فاعل in the sense of مفعول when it is a naʿt (adjective), as in «ماء دافق» and سرّ كاتم, i.e. a concealed (مكتوم) secret. Abū Jaʿfar said: فاعل in the sense of مفعول destroys clarity; it is not sound and not subject to analogy. If this were permissible, ضارب ("striker") would be permissible in the sense of مضروب ("struck"). The view of the Basrans is that it is on [the pattern of] relation (nasab), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 555- كليني لهم يا أميمة ناصب (Leave me, O Umayma, to a wearisome care), and as [another] said: [al-ṭawīl] 556-
وليس بذي سيف فيقتلني به ... وليس بذي رمح وليس بنبّال ]
(He is not one with a sword, that he should kill me with it, nor one with a spear, nor an archer.) [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears at the end of the verse in the source.]

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
ʿĪsā read مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلُبِ [Translator's note: the source prints «الصُّلْبِ», the standard reading; ʿĪsā's variant is presumably «الصُّلُب», as the following remark suggests.], and al-Aṣmaʿī reported: الصُّلُب is in the sense of الصُّلْب.
وَالتَّرائِبِ is the plural of تريبة [Translator's note: the source reads «تربية», a misprint]; one also says تريب. The scholars differed about its meaning. Among the soundest that has been said about it is what ʿAṭiyya related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الترائب is the place of the necklace. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الترائب is [what is] between the woman's breasts. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: الترائب are the ribs down to the bottom of the backbone. Mujāhid said: what is between the shoulders and the chest. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الترائب are the hands, the feet and the eyes. Qatāda said: الترائب is towards the backbone. Al-Layth ibn Saʿd related from Maʿmar ibn Abī Ḥabība, who said: الترائب is the freshness (marrow) of the heart, and from it comes the child. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because it is related that the fluid comes out from the whole body, even from every hair; but the first view is the one used in the speech of the Arabs, as the poet said: [al-wāfir] 557-
ومن ذهب يلوح على تريب ... كلون العاج ليس بذي غضون
(And of gold gleaming on an upper breast, like the colour of ivory, without wrinkles.)
And as [another] said: [al-ṭawīl] 558-
مهفهفة بيضاء غير مفاضة ... ترائبها مصقولة كالسّجنجل
(Slender-waisted, fair, not flabby-bellied, her breastbones polished like a mirror.)
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning of "between the backbone and the breastbones" is "from the backbone and the breastbones"; he does not make بين redundant, but [it is] as one says: فلان هالك بين هذين ("so-and-so is perishing between these two").

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
The scholars differed about this pronoun. Among the soundest that has been said about it is the view of Qatāda, who said: [He is able] to resurrect him and bring him back; on this [view] the pronoun is for man. Abū Jaʿfar said: It was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād, from Mindal ibn ʿAlī, from Layth, from Mujāhid, concerning إِنَّهُ عَلى رَجْعِهِ لَقادِرٌ: he said: [able] to return the fluid into the urethra. This is the school of Ibn Zayd; he said: على رجعه لقادر — able to hold it back so that it does not come out. These are two views, and from al-Ḍaḥḥāk [something] like their meaning; and from him a third view: على رجعه لقادر — he said: [able] to return him after old age to youth, after youth to childhood, and after childhood to the sperm-drop. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is the clearer of them; Muḥammad ibn Jarīr chose it, except that he used an argument to strengthen it which is a mistake in Arabic. He claimed that His saying, the Exalted, يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرائِرُ belongs to the ṣila (completion) of رجعه, interpreting it as "He is able to bring him back on the day the secrets are tested". Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a mistake. If it were so, it would enter into the ṣila of رجعه, and you would be separating the ṣila from what it completes by the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and that is not permissible. Rather, «يوم» is governed by ناصر.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t:
[تُبْلَى means] they are tested and made manifest. It was said: it means the prayer, the fasting and the ritual bath after major impurity.
فَما لَهُ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ: Qatāda said: [no] strength to protect him from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; وَلا ناصِرٍ to help him against Him. Al-Thawrī said: مِنْ قُوَّةٍ — of kinsfolk; وَلا ناصِرٍ — an ally.
